cards.question: How is severe acute asthma treated in ICU?
cards.answer: Correct life-threatening hypoxia immediately with 100% oxygen, then titrate to SpO₂ 94–98% after stabilisation (UK BTS/SIGN). Back-to-back salbutamol/ipratropium nebs, IV hydrocortisone 100 mg, IV magnesium 2 g over 20 min; specialist escalation to IV salbutamol or aminophylline; intubate for exhaustion, silent chest or PaCO₂ rising despite treatment.

cards.question: What ventilator strategy minimises gas trapping in severe asthma?
cards.answer: Low rate (8–10/min), Vt 6 mL/kg, long expiratory time (I:E ≥1:4), permit hypercapnia (pH ≥7.20), apply minimal PEEP (3–5) below intrinsic PEEP, and use heavy sedation ± paralysis to prevent dyssynchrony.

cards.question: When should ECMO be considered in life-threatening asthma?
cards.answer: Refractory hypercapnia (pH <7.20), dynamic hyperinflation with haemodynamic compromise, or barotrauma; VV-ECMO allows lung rest and CO₂ clearance with reported survival >80% in this group (ELSO registry).
